articles.title: AITO Looks Ahead to Europe, Building a Thriving Automotive Ecosystem
articles.content: AITO Looks Ahead to Europe, Building a Thriving Automotive Ecosystem | ZAWYA AITO Looks Ahead to Europe, Building a Thriving Automotive Ecosystem Seres Group Co., Ltd. | Asia Press Release - 18 October 2026 - At the 2026 Paris Motor Show, Clifford Kang, Board Member and Vice President of SERES Group, announced that AITO plans to officially enter the European market in autumn 2027, marking another major step in its global development. With deep respect for Europe's automotive heritage, AITO looks forward to collaborating and growing with partners around the world. https://youtu.be/6Zoz_hxLRxk?si=948OAjqPhndVNE7J In China, AITO has earned the trust of over 1.2 million customers. Globally, in Brand Finance's Automobiles 100 2026 ranking, AITO ranked among the world's top 10 luxury automotive brands and was the No.1 Chinese luxury automotive brand by brand value, making it the only Chinese automotive brand. Driven by its philosophy of "Intelligence Redefining Luxury", AITO is committed to bringing together traditional luxury and technological luxury to create an elevated intelligent mobility experience. "AITO stands for 'Adding Intelligence to Auto'. We believe a vehicle should be a mobile intelligent agent that understands you and responds to your needs. That is why we introduced our brand philosophy, Intelligence Redefining Luxury. It is our interpretation of what New Luxury means for AITO," said Clifford Kang, Board Member and Vice President of SERES Group . "We come with deep respect for Europe's automotive heritage. We come to collaborate and grow with partners around the world. And we come with our philosophy: Intelligence Redefining Luxury." As AITO strengthens its global presence, it looks forward to working with partners across the value chain to build a healthy automotive ecosystem, foster mutual growth and bring intelligent luxury mobility to more customers around the world. articles.title: Sustainable Energy Research Centre Laboratory opened at SQU
articles.desc: Muscat: The Sustainable Energy Research Centre Laboratory at Sultan Qaboos University (SQU) was opened on Sunday in a step that enhances integration between...
articles.content: Sustainable Energy Research Centre Laboratory opened at SQU - Times of Oman Sustainable Energy Research Centre Laboratory opened at SQU Muscat: The Sustainable Energy Research Centre Laboratory at Sultan Qaboos University (SQU) was opened on Sunday in a step that enhances integration between scientific research, innovation, and national capacity building. The opening was held under the auspices of Eng. Salim Nasser Al Aufi, Minister of Energy and Minerals. The opening of the Sustainable Energy Research Centre Laboratory comes as a fruit of the strategic partnership between Sultan Qaboos University and Oxy Oman, with a total investment of nearly OMR1.5 million across an area of approximately 774 square meters. It constitutes a qualitative addition to the national research infrastructure and an integrated platform for developing innovative technologies and solutions in sustainable energy fields, strengthening research and technical capabilities, and supporting cooperation between academic and industrial institutions. The laboratory comprises a set of specialised research units, including alternative fuels, energy materials, energy efficiency, thermal energy, carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS) and hydrogen, a smart grids and renewable energy systems modeling and simulation laboratory, and a dedicated studio for training and capacity building, allowing scientific research to be utilized in developing practical solutions that support sector efficiency and sustainability. In a related context, the Ministry of Energy and Minerals, represented by Oman Sustainability Centre, and Sultan Qaboos University signed an agreement to execute the second edition of the “Kafa’a” (Efficiency) training program for a duration of three years. The agreement was signed by Eng. Salim Nasser Al Aufi, Minister of Energy and Minerals, and HH Sayyid Dr. Fahad Al Julanda Al Said, Vice-Chancellor of Sultan Qaboos University. It aims to expand the scope of specialised professional qualification in energy efficiency and connect training outputs with practical application, entrepreneurship, and market needs. The agreement aims to train and qualify 275 participants in energy auditing and 20 participants in measurement and verification, as well as incubate at least three national teams—each consisting of four members—and support them to develop solutions and services and establish startups specialized in energy efficiency. This contributes to building a national base of professional expertise, developing a local market for specialised services, and creating new economic and job opportunities. The Minister of Energy and Minerals, emphasized that investing in scientific research, innovation, and national capacity building represents a strategic pillar for developing the energy sector and enhancing its competitiveness and sustainability. He pointed out the importance of integrating efforts among government, academic, and private sector institutions in developing innovative technologies and solutions, as well as building national capabilities capable of deploying them to develop the sector and keep pace with its future transformations. Al Aufi explained that the opening of the Sustainable Energy Research Centre Laboratory and the renewal of the “Kafa’a” training program agreement reflect this orientation by connecting scientific research with practical application, as well as qualifying Omani talents and empowering them to utilize scientific research outputs and specialised knowledge in creating new investment and economic opportunities. This enhances entrepreneurship and local content (in-country value), while contributing to raising energy consumption efficiency and reducing emissions in support of the targets of Oman Vision 2040 and net-zero emissions by 2050.
